newsitem.title: USA: OTR Express sees wider Q4 loss.
newsitem.headline: OTR Express sees wider Q4 loss.

text.p: OTR Express Inc, a long-haul truckload carrier, said on Wednesday that high fuel costs and unmanned trucks adversely impacted financial results for the fourth quarter ended December 31, 1996.
OTR said it expects to report a higher net loss than the loss of $88,000, or $0.05 a share, in the fourth quarter of 1995.
Actual results for the quarter will be released on February 11.
"The expected loss is a disappointment for the company, considering our recent progress with consecutive positive quarters," said William Ward, president and chief executive officer, in a statement.

"Diesel fuel prices in the fourth quarter were at the highest levels in more than five years. We implemented a fuel surcharge to customers in October to share a portion of the additional cost and soften the impact. However, the net cost was still enough to reduce fourth quarter earnings below anticipated levels," he said.

The market for qualified drivers remains very competitive. The company said it tried to keep the trucks manned without an across-the-board increase in driver wage rates. The result was an unmanned trucks percentage of 6.2 percent in the fourth quarter, which was higher than anticipated and reduced miles per unit per week.

OTR said it is addressing these issues. Fuel prices have moderated, easing to $1.21 per gallon compared to a fourth-quarter average of $1.28. At this level, the additional fuel cost is being recovered through fuel surcharges and a fuel hedging program.
OTR said it is implementing new programs to reduce the number of unmanned trucks by expanding the base of potential new drivers, including teams and regional drivers.
In 1996, low miles contributed to a higher turnover of the driver fleet. OTR said this year it will focus on utilization of the equipment to minimize driver turnover.

The company reported a revenue rate per mile of $0.994 in the fourth quarter, a significant increase from the rate of $0.957 in the fourth quarter of 1995. Utilization was 2,007 miles per week per unit compared with 1,959 in 1995.

Ward said the company is entering the traditionally slow months of January and February with 65 percent shipper freight and 35 percent broker freight, which is a much stronger position than the 50/50 mix at this time last year. This should improve both utilization and the revenue rate for the first quarter, he said.

OTR also said Gary Klusman was named chief operating officer and Eric Janzen was named vice president marketing. Klusman has previously been chief financial officer and most recently was executive vice president. Janzen has served as an account executive and has been the director of marketing for two years.
